Stage 4 — model pilot

Proves the training pipeline runs end to end. A reduced subset (8,000 train / 3,000 val windows), not a performance result.

modelparamsbest epochepochs runbest val lossthresholdval accval sensval specval prec
proposed217602130.580.110.089710.00070.0891
ecg_only75906440.61930.1550.21530.90640.14780.0941
resp_only74946440.67860.2150.35070.74910.31170.0961
simple_fusion150658240.63710.0950.091310.00260.0892
Training loss fell in all four models, gradients were finite, and reloaded checkpoints reproduced identical logits. What the pilot also showed is that the models memorise subjects: train AUC ≈0.80 against pooled validation AUC 0.45–0.56, with per-subject validation AUC varying from 0.33 to 0.87. That is a regularisation/budget problem for Stage 5, not a bug: labels, shapes, normalisation, and signal reads were all verified.

Full data improved generalisation over the pilot (proposed AUC 0.467 → 0.644; simple fusion 0.498 → 0.693), but two things must be said plainly: proposed did not beat simple_fusion on validation (0.644 vs 0.693), and the PSG validation AUC is below 0.5 for every model — only two PSG subjects, one of them with no positive windows, so that number carries no evidence. Thresholds found by F1 are low (0.095–0.37) with precision 0.10–0.14 at 8.9% prevalence, i.e. the models lean towards predicting positive.

AUC decomposition — pooled vs per subject

modelpooled AUCmean subject AUCmin subject AUCmax subject AUCwithin-subject AUCsubjects scored
resp_only0.73450.74840.63540.8330.71216
proposed0.52610.73280.53030.85240.6726

ecg_only0.3590.55370.4270.6180.50516
For proposed the pooled AUC is 0.526 while the mean per-subject AUC is 0.733. That 0.21 gap is a cross-subject calibration failure: each subject gets a differently offset score scale, so ranking breaks when all windows are pooled. resp_only is the only model where pooled and per-subject AUC agree. This decomposition is a diagnostic, not a headline metric, and the pooled figure is the one that must be reported.

All four UCDDB subjects are above 0.69, but the two PSG subjects are lower (slp02 weakest at 0.53). With six subjects, the pooled test figure is one measurement, not a performance estimate.
Must be reported, not buried: resp_only is the best model on test (AUC 0.734) and proposed is second (0.526). The cross-attention architecture has not been shown to help. ecg_only collapses on UCDDB (specificity 0.044), and thresholds carried over from validation do not transfer optimally (precision 0.11–0.21 at 14.7% prevalence) — they were deliberately not retuned after seeing test.

Stage 6b — calibration diagnostic

Post-hoc diagnostic, not a protocol. Run after the test results were seen, so nothing here may be used to select a model or replace the headline metric. The reported metric stays the pooled AUC with the frozen validation threshold.

Is the offset a model property or a test-subject property?

modelsplitsubjectsSpearmanpleave-one-out range
proposedval60.0290.957[-0.2, 0.8]
proposedtest6-0.9430.005[-1.0, -0.9]
simple_fusionval60.2570.623[-0.1, 0.8]
simple_fusiontest6-0.2570.623[-0.5, 0.3]
ecg_onlyval6-0.2570.623[-0.5, 0.3]

Do not overclaim. The correlation is −0.943 on test (p = 0.005, stable under leave-one-out) but only +0.029 on validation (p = 0.957). So the inversion belongs to the six test subjects, not to the model as a stable trait. What is already visible on validation is slp41: zero positive windows, yet the highest mean score in the whole validation split (0.504, above slp23 at 12.7% and slp03 at 33.5%). A subject with one class has no defined AUC, so it never appears in any AUC table and never triggered a warning.
Prior inversion, test only. Subject 22 has the lowest prevalence (1.9%) but the highest mean score (0.450), so 70.9% of its windows are called positive. That is the mechanism destroying the pooled AUC, not an inability to rank within a subject (within-subject AUC 0.672). Leave-one-out leaves the correlation between −0.90 and −1.00 on test, but it does not replicate on validation — see the table above.

Stage 6c — per-record offset probe

Hypothesis tested and rejected. If dataset-level normalisation left each record with its own mean offset, that offset would be a record-level shortcut the model could exploit. It does not: the post-normalisation mean is 0.00 for all 39 records in both modalities, because the signals were detrended before z-scoring.

What was found instead: per-record scale is not uniform

datasetrecordECG std (z units)resp std (z units)ECG clippedresp clipped
MIT-BIH_PSGslp02b0.6765.9210.000540.1037
MIT-BIH_PSGslp02a0.7055.2590.000850.07976
MIT-BIH_PSGslp031.5492.4710.029950.03663
MIT-BIH_PSGslp320.9891.6290.012510.01701
MIT-BIH_PSGslp410.7221.1320.000650.01508
MIT-BIH_PSGslp600.991.4560.016290.00807
MIT-BIH_PSGslp481.0911.1360.008490.00583
MIT-BIH_PSGslp451.3530.7720.018240.00142
MIT-BIH_PSGslp370.6210.54900.00084
MIT-BIH_PSGslp660.5870.72700.00033
The ±5σ clip does not act equally on every record. Averaged over all 39 records, 1.16% of ECG samples and 0.69% of respiration samples are clipped. The worst records lose far more: slp02b 10.4% of its respiration. This corrects an earlier claim in this report and in the work log that clipping was "almost never active (0.1% of ECG)" — that figure was wrong. Because per-record scale varies from 0.55 to 5.92 (dataset std units), the same 5σ threshold bites very differently per recording.

Still open (Experiments 2–4): 30 s window comparison, preprocessing ablation, and single- vs combined-dataset training with LODO. Also open: the ECG-only Apnea-ECG arm. No results in this report cover those.

Decisions & exclusions

itemreason
Apnea-ECGECG-only: all 70 base records contain a single ECG channel at 100 Hz; no respiratory channel.
ucddb005Flow channel unusable: std 0.503 vs 4.2-6.0 in other UCDDB records, only 318 unique values, flat after initial transient. Excluded rather than substituted with an effort channel, preserving the strict airflow policy.
slp01a, slp01bStrict airflow policy: only Resp (sum) available.
slp61Strict airflow policy: only Resp (abdominal) available.

Label rule: a window is positive when at least 50% of its duration overlaps an annotated apnea or hypopnea event. PSG labels inherit 30 s epochs, so 10 s windows carry coarse (weak) labels; this is reported as label noise rather than corrected.

Decisions taken so far

#DecisionWhyBasis
1Apnea-ECG excluded from multimodal (ECG-only arm only)It does have ECG, which is required, but no respiratory channel. The multimodal model consumes ECG and respiration for the same window, so one modality is not enough. Still usable for the ECG-only arm.Sec. 3.3 (availability verified by audit); Sec. 3.4.2
2Strict airflow channel policyUCDDB Flow (thermistor) matched to PSG Resp (nasal); mixing airflow with effort is not equivalentSec. 3.4.2
3slp01a, slp01b excludedOnly Resp (sum) is availableconsequence of #2
4slp61 excludedOnly Resp (abdominal) is availableconsequence of #2
5ucddb005 excludedDead Flow channel: std 0.50 vs 4.2-6.0 elsewhere, 318 unique values, flat for ~6 hchannel audit
6Positive = apnea OR hypopneaPaper labeling ruleSec. 3.4.4
7POSSIBLE and PB EVENT are not positiveAmbiguous events; counting them would inflate positives without supportSec. 3.4.4
8Window positive at >=50% overlapPaper labeling ruleSec. 3.4.4
9Train overlapping, val/test non-overlappingPaper protocolSec. 3.4.4
10Windows only inside annotated regionsUnannotated intervals must not be labelled normalcontext §6-7
11Tail truncated, not paddedAvoid fabricating samplesimplementation choice (paper: TBD)
12z-score fitted per dataset from training windows onlyNo test statistics leak; dataset scales differ ~22xSec. 3.4.3
13ECG 100 Hz, respiration 25 HzModerate cost, safe cut-offsprovisional (paper defers to audit)
14Clipping at c = 5 sigmaLimit motion artefacts without cutting normal signalprovisional

Limitations that must be reported

LimitationDetail
Thin evaluation unit, not few windowsTest has 6 subjects (4 UCDDB + 2 PSG). Autocorrelation-adjusted N_eff is ~1875 (UCDDB) and ~110 (PSG); test contains ~583 contiguous positive runs.
Uneven positive distribution across test subjectsSeed 42: UCDDB subject 22 has 1.9% positive windows, PSG subject slp16 has 42.5%.
PSG labels are coarse30 s epoch labels inherited by 10 s windows; reported as label noise, not corrected.
50% threshold is sensitive for UCDDB at 30 s~10k windows fall in the 0.4-0.6 overlap band, peaking exactly at 0.5.
LODO is two-way onlyUCDDB<->PSG, because the third dataset fails the channel requirement.
Clipping at 5 sigma is not uniform across records; an earlier figure was wrongRecomputed over all 39 records: 1.16% of ECG samples and 0.69% of respiration samples are clipped on average — not the 0.1% stated earlier. Worst cases lose 10.4% (slp02b) and 8.0% (slp02a) of respiration. Per-record scale ranges 0.55–5.92 in dataset-std units, so the same threshold bites very differently. The clipping ablation is therefore meaningful, and the choice must be made before retraining.
PSG respiration is uncalibratedAmplitude carries no physiological units; z-scoring makes it usable but not interpretable.
Proposed architecture is not supported by the resultsAcross three seeds, test AUC for proposed is 0.526 / 0.552 / 0.586 (mean 0.555 ± 0.030) while the respiration-only baseline scores 0.734 / 0.751 / 0.742 (0.742 ± 0.008). Proposed loses in every seed. No evidence that cross-attention helps.
Cross-subject score calibration is unresolved; mechanism only partly measuredProposed: gap 0.044 on validation, 0.207 on test. On test Spearman(prevalence, mean score) = −0.943 (p=0.005, stable under leave-one-out; subject 22 has the lowest prevalence 1.9% and the highest mean score 0.450), but on validation it is +0.029 (p=0.957). The inversion is a property of the six test subjects, not of the model as a stable trait. The stronger warning sign is slp41 on validation: 0% prevalence with the highest mean score (0.504), invisible because a single-class subject has no defined AUC.
Per-record score normalisation is a post-hoc rescue, not a resultz-scoring per record lifts test AUC 0.526 → 0.671 for proposed but lowers validation 0.644 → 0.601. It was chosen after seeing test and hurts the split not used to choose it, so it must not be reported as the headline metric.
Three seeds, one window durationModel comparison (Experiment 1) now has 3 seeds at 10 s, reported as mean ± SD. The 30 s condition (Experiment 2), preprocessing ablation (Experiment 3), and single- vs combined-dataset training plus LODO (Experiment 4) have not been run.
SD across seeds is split sensitivity, not run-to-run varianceEach seed is a different subject-level split, so the SD measures how much the conclusion depends on which subjects land in validation/test. With 6 test subjects, the SD for proposed (0.030) is narrower than its own bootstrap CI (0.41–0.81), so small model differences cannot be resolved by this data.
